events.what: Bérczi uses AlphaEvolve to evolve candidate ranking functions for a toy model of canonical blow-ups (dim 4, char 3) and states two conjectures
events.ai_basis: Scope none, so it cannot set the status. AlphaEvolve did produce the candidate ranking-function code, but those candidates are heuristics for a toy simulator, not mathematics in a result on the bullet.

events.what: Tian, arXiv:2608.20066 (798 pp.), claims canonical strong embedded resolution over any perfect field of characteristic p>0 in all dimensions
events.credibility_reason: Several F5-type signals: landmark problem, author affiliated with a Princeton infrastructure-systems lab rather than mathematics, heavy coined terminology absent from the literature, no known prior work in the area. But the preprint is only about one month old at the record's check date, too short a time for the required 'no uptake over a long enough period' signal, and no specific error has been identified. So it is kept as doubtful rather than set aside.
events.ai_basis: The record only suspects AI authorship from the writing style. No disclosure or source credits an AI system.

judgement.doubts: This is a close call between doubtful and not_credible for Tian. By the time a later pass runs, the missing-uptake signal may well be met, and this should then drop to open. The researcher excluded the claim under an older rule. The Bérczi paper states conjectures about a toy model and bounds nothing, so the old 'progress' code had no basis in any case. Any suspicion that Tian's text is AI-generated is unconfirmed.

outcome_prefix: Judged: status rests on Tian's August 2026 preprint arXiv:2608.20066, an unreviewed and doubtful claim of full resolution in characteristic p; the Bérczi AlphaEvolve paper is exploratory and settles or bounds nothing.

corrections.why: F5 (not over-applied): the record's evidence against 2608.20066 is suggestive, but the paper is about one month old with no identified error, so it is doubtful, not set aside. The record says it 'claims a full canonical strong embedded resolution … over any perfect field of characteristic p>0', so the scope is whole, and unreviewed means claimed. Bérczi's paper 'states two conjectures, not a proof' about a toy model, so its scope is none and it cannot give progress.

F8: the status now rests on Tian's preprint, and no source credits an AI system with it. Suspected AI authorship is only inferred from style. The AlphaEvolve quote stays in place but belongs to the Bérczi event, which was discarded.
other: the claimed event asserts that resolution exists, as conjectured.
